candidates.title: The Post-Caller
candidates.premise:
Nate Cairns is twenty-six, has half a physics degree, and spent four years running sound for bands in bars. His one real trick: when a speaker started to howl, he killed the howl by feeding in a second sound shaped to cancel the first.

He is now in a stone city where people take buildings apart by finding the single beat a thing answers to — every solid thing has one — and holding that beat until the thing shakes itself to pieces. They call themselves callers. Against them are the packers, who build in mismatched layers of stone, reed and river mud so a wall answers nothing at all, and who can end a call by laying a hand on the caller doing it. A body is supposed to hold one craft or the other, never both.

Nate holds both, because cancelling is packing done with sound. He can walk up to a wall no caller can touch and hum it dead. It costs him a full day afterward, in which he cannot hear the beat of anything and is an ordinary man, and both schools know it.

Callers are named for the biggest thing they can bring down: cup, post, wall, span, hill. Nate is a post. The yard that trains him wants the old bridge, which no caller has ever taken.

records.subject: sys_the_answer
records.value: system

records.subject: sys_the_answer
records.value: Every solid thing answers at one beat, set by what it is made of and how big it is. Push in time with that beat and each push adds to the last until the thing tears itself apart. Push harder but out of time and nothing happens at all. So the craft is not strength, it is patience and accuracy: find the beat, then hold it while the world tries to stop you.

records.subject: sys_the_answer
records.value: A caller stands with a flat palm on a gate, humming one low note, and after a minute the hinges begin to knock back at her in time.

records.subject: sys_the_answer
records.value: On open ground and at any distance the caller wins: a packer must be within arm's reach to do anything, and a wall-caller can drop a gate from across a yard. Inside anything a packer built, the packer wins absolutely — a packed wall answers nothing and no caller of any name has ever taken one. Hand to hand, the packer wins: a hand laid flat on a calling caller kills the note dead. Children are made to choose at twelve, at the yard's wall, and the choice is physical rather than sworn — a year of packing work leaves a body unable to hear the answer ever again, and no one has come back from it. What a caller can do that a packer never can is take a thing down from far away. What a packer can do that a caller never can is make a thing that cannot be taken at all.

records.subject: sys_the_answer_nature
records.value: The answer is indifferent. It has no side and takes no notice of who is holding the beat, which is why the old bridge has beaten everybody who ever tried.

records.subject: sys_the_answer_view
records.value: view

records.subject: sys_the_answer_view
records.value: A caller stands with a flat palm on a gate, humming one low note, and after a minute the hinges begin to knock back at her in time.

records.subject: sys_the_answer_view
records.value: Nothing tells a caller what a thing answers at. You find it by hand, by ear, by wasting an afternoon.

records.subject: rule_one_beat
records.value: Every solid thing answers at one beat, set by what it is made of and how big it is. Find it, push in time, and the thing comes apart. Push out of time, however hard, and nothing happens.

records.subject: rule_one_beat
records.value: He lays his hand flat on a cart axle and hums until the hum comes back at him louder than he made it, and the axle jumps out of its bed.

records.subject: rule_one_beat
records.value: Nobody builds anything to one size any more. Good stonework runs in courses of different thicknesses on purpose, and a mason who cuts a hundred matching blocks is laughed out of the yard.

records.subject: rule_one_beat
records.value: Armies never march in step. Officers set an uneven count on purpose, and a column that falls into a rhythm crossing a bridge is stopped and shouted at.

records.subject: rule_one_beat
records.value: Children are taught which rooms not to sing in. Stone stairwells and cellar arches are quiet places by custom, and a man humming in one gets stared at the way a man striking matches in a barn does.

records.subject: rule_the_hold_takes_time
records.value: Nothing goes on the first push. The beat has to be held while the thing takes it, and the bigger the thing the longer the hold. A caller in the middle of a hold cannot do anything else, cannot move much, and cannot defend themselves.

records.subject: rule_the_hold_takes_time
records.value: She kneels with both hands on the gate and a boy stands over her with a stave, watching the street, while she counts through her teeth.

records.subject: rule_the_hold_takes_time
records.value: House-breakers keep a cup-caller for locks and a second body to stand over them, so burglary is a two-person trade and locks are now made of two metals fitted together so they answer at nothing.

records.subject: rule_the_hold_takes_time
records.value: To buy one caller a full minute on a gate an army spends bodies in front of her, and every siege plan is really a plan about a minute.

records.subject: rule_the_hold_takes_time
records.value: The long hold has become a prayer. Their word for patience and their word for the hold are the same word, and mourners sit with a hand on a stone for as long as the dead person's age in breaths.

records.subject: rule_a_body_answers_too
records.value: A living body has a beat like anything else, but it moves — every breath and every heartbeat shifts it — so it cannot be held long enough to matter unless the caller is at hill.

records.subject: rule_a_body_answers_too
records.value: A guard walking a nervous street breathes deliberately raggedly and hums flat and tuneless, the way people whistle in the dark.

records.subject: rule_a_body_answers_too
records.value: Frightened people breathe on purpose out of rhythm, and a man doing it in a market is a man who thinks somebody is after him, which everyone can see.

records.subject: rule_a_body_answers_too
records.value: Bodyguards are trained to hum tunelessly and constantly around whoever they are guarding, so no note near them ever settles, and a quiet bodyguard is a bribed one.

records.subject: rule_a_body_answers_too
records.value: No ordinary men can hold a hill-caller, so cities keep packers on their gates instead of soldiers, and the packing house has quietly become the thing that decides who walks in.

records.subject: cup
records.value: Water in a glass beside them shivers when they breathe. They keep the first cup they ever cracked on their belt, in three pieces on a wire.

records.subject: cup
records.value: A season of standing with a hand on things until they answer, and everything breakable they own is broken by the end of it. The hand they learn with goes clumsy for months and they eat left-handed in front of everybody.

records.subject: cup
records.value: Bring apart anything they can close a hand around: snap the pin in a lock, split a stone, crack ice, take the ring off a seized bolt. It works through a door if they can touch the door.

records.subject: post
records.value: Doors rattle in their frames as they walk past, and shopkeepers put a hand on their shutters when they come up the street.

records.subject: post
records.value: They must take down a roof post while standing under it, with the yard watching, and not step out. Some do not step out fast enough.

records.subject: post
records.value: Bring down anything one person could carry or lean on — a door, a cart axle, a spear in a man's hands, a ladder under a climber — from a few paces away, and take a good half-minute doing it.

records.subject: wall
records.value: Dust falls out of a ceiling when they walk under it, and the sand in the street is smooth and stoneless wherever they have stood a while.

records.subject: wall
records.value: They stand inside the shadow of the wall they are taking until it goes. Everyone who does it comes out with their ears ringing so hard they hear nothing at all for three days, and in those three days anybody at all can come up behind them.

records.subject: wall
records.value: Drop a house wall or a gate from across a yard, and hold a wall standing through a shake that should have laid it flat.

records.subject: span
records.value: Birds leave a roof before they get to it. Horses will not stand still under them.

records.subject: span
records.value: The yard puts their own teacher out on the span and makes them take it. Whoever is on the bridge remembers it, and half of them never speak to the caller again.

records.subject: span
records.value: Take a bridge out from under a marching column, or hold one up while their own people cross it, from far enough away that nobody can reach them in time.

records.subject: hill
records.value: Glass rings when they enter a room. Sleeping people wake as they pass the bed. The ground around them is always bare of small stones, because everything loose has walked itself away.

records.subject: hill
records.value: After it, nothing fine near them is ever quiet again. They cannot sit with anyone frail, cannot hold a newborn, cannot sleep in a house with anybody else in it. And the packing house stops trying to recruit them and starts trying to pack them.

records.subject: hill
records.value: Bring a cliff face down into a valley, hold a whole town's stone together while the ground moves under it, and — because a living body has a beat too, if you can hold it — stop a man dead where he stands, across a field, without touching him.

records.subject: sys_packing
records.value: system

records.subject: sys_packing
records.value: A thing made of mismatched layers has no single beat. The push spreads out through stone, reed, mud and lead thread, each of which answers at something different, and it dies before it can add to itself. So the packers do not fight a call, they make a thing that cannot be called. Their whole craft is layering, and their creed is that anything with one clean beat is a thing already waiting to fall down.

records.subject: sys_packing
records.value: A grey striped wall, ugly as a wasp's nest, with reed ends and river mud showing between the courses — and a caller standing in front of it for an hour with nothing at all happening.

records.subject: sys_packing
records.value: See the calling side of it: distance and open ground go to the caller, arm's reach and packed ground go to the packer, and no body has ever held both crafts.

records.subject: sys_packing_nature
records.value: The packing house believes it is the only reason the city is still standing, and it is not entirely wrong.

records.subject: sys_packing_view
records.value: view

records.subject: sys_packing_view
records.value: A grey striped wall, ugly as a wasp's nest, with reed ends and river mud showing between the courses — and a caller standing in front of it for an hour with nothing at all happening.

records.subject: sys_packing_view
records.value: From the outside there is no way to tell a packed wall from a plain one until a caller has already wasted an hour on it. Packers like it that way.

records.subject: rule_layers_have_no_beat
records.value: Build a thing in alternating layers of unlike stuff — stone, reed, mud, lead thread — and it answers at no single beat. No caller of any name can take it.

records.subject: rule_layers_have_no_beat
records.value: A packer thumbs a wet reed mat down between two stone courses, slaps mud over it, and says nothing while the caller she beat that morning watches from the road.

records.subject: rule_layers_have_no_beat
records.value: Packed houses are hot, dark and thick-walled, and every home in the city smells faintly of wet reed. Anyone who grew up poor grew up in that smell and knows a packed room by nose in the dark.

records.subject: rule_layers_have_no_beat
records.value: A packed gate cannot be called down, so sieges are back to ladders, fire and starving people out, and a war now takes a season instead of an afternoon.

records.subject: rule_layers_have_no_beat
records.value: Anything worth stealing lives in a packed room, so thieves have stopped calling locks and started digging under floors, and the city's cellars are full of holes nobody admits to.

records.subject: rule_a_packed_person
records.value: A person can be packed too: a layered harness of hide, reed and lead thread worn under the clothes for months until the body under it answers at nothing. While it is on, no caller can touch them.

records.subject: rule_a_packed_person
records.value: He unbuttons his coat to show the grey mat underneath, and when he reaches out to shake a hand the hand does not close properly.

records.subject: rule_a_packed_person
records.value: Every ruler in the city wears one, so every ruler in the city is visibly slow, and the way you spot power in a crowd is by who moves like a man wading.

records.subject: rule_a_packed_person
records.value: A packed man cannot feel a fever in his own child's forehead and cannot swim in the river, so the wealthy do not go near water and their children are checked by servants.

records.subject: rule_a_packed_person
records.value: The front rank of any column is packed men who cannot run, which is why a charge in this city walks.

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: agency

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: A beat coming out of the ground under the hill, too low for any ear, that never stops.

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: Nothing. It is not a person and has never been one.

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: A day's walk in every direction, and further in bad weather.

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: Anybody who calls within a day's walk of it, whose note it takes up and continues after they stop.

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: A caller working near it never has to hold — the beat is held for them — and can take something four names above their own.

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: Everything they take stays taking. A wall dropped near the hill goes on coming apart for weeks, and so does the house behind it, and so does the road.

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: He stops humming and the wall keeps going anyway, faster, and he cannot make it stop.

records.subject: the_low_beat
records.value: Nobody has dug down to find out, because digging there is how the last three parties died.

records.subject: the_low_beat_belief
records.value: Everyone believes it is the ruin of the old capital settling.

records.subject: the_low_beat_secret
records.value: It is getting louder, at about the rate a man's hair goes grey, and stack city is inside the edge of it now.

records.subject: the_ringing_bar
records.value: carrier

records.subject: the_ringing_bar
records.value: A forearm of soft iron that holds a found beat for about a day.

records.subject: the_ringing_bar
records.value: Anybody at all can use a beat somebody else found, which is how a cup-caller opens a strongroom lock a wall-caller found for them.

records.subject: the_ringing_bar
records.value: Whoever put the beat in cannot call anything until it is used up, so a crew that carries bars is a crew with one member deliberately made useless.

records.subject: the_ringing_bar
records.value: A warm bar in a boy's satchel that faintly hums against his ribs all afternoon and goes cold and quiet the moment it is spent.

records.subject: the_ringing_bar
records.value: He has never dropped one, and he has been offered money for one twice.

records.subject: the_ringing_bar_secret
records.value: A bar that has held a beat too long takes a second one badly, and three of the yard's bars are already lying about what they hold.

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: cast

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: Twenty-six, half a physics degree, four years running sound in bars, and now a post-caller in a city he cannot find on any map.

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: To get to hill, and to know what reached for him.

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: Talks like a man explaining a mixing desk to somebody who did not ask: short, flat, one joke too many when he is frightened.

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: He listens to a room before he looks at it, and he taps things — tables, walls, his own cup — without noticing he does it.

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: She took him in because he could find a beat in one afternoon, and she has not told him what she wants him for.

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: She got to wall the hard way, standing in the shadow of it, and he skipped every step she bled for.

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: Oam saw him cancel a wall and understood immediately what it means for the packing house.

records.subject: nate_cairns
records.value: The boy stands over him while he holds, carries the bar, and has never once run.

records.subject: nate_cairns_belief
records.value: That because both crafts come easy to him, one of the two schools will eventually decide he is worth protecting.

records.subject: nate_cairns_secret
records.value: He has already tried to cancel a person and it worked for a second and a half, and he has told nobody.

records.subject: soll_ivry
records.value: cast

records.subject: soll_ivry
records.value: A span-caller who runs the yard where callers are trained, and the only person alive who has taken a bridge with somebody standing on it.

records.subject: soll_ivry
records.value: The old bridge down before she dies, because she has been told her whole life it cannot be done.

records.subject: soll_ivry
records.value: Short sentences, never raises her voice, ends instructions with the price of getting them wrong.

records.subject: soll_ivry
records.value: Birds go off a roof before she reaches it, and the horse at the yard gate will not stand still while she talks.

records.subject: soll_ivry
records.value: She has already decided he is the one who takes the bridge, and has not said so.

records.subject: soll_ivry
records.value: She was the one who fetched the packers the night Wend went silent.

records.subject: soll_ivry
records.value: He was at the gate that night and did nothing, which is not quite true.

records.subject: soll_ivry_belief
records.value: That the bridge has beaten callers because none of them were strong enough.

records.subject: soll_ivry_secret
records.value: Her older sister is alive, teaches in the packing house under another name, and Soll goes to see her twice a year.

records.subject: dessa_kern
records.value: cast

records.subject: dessa_kern
records.value: Nineteen, the fastest anyone has gone from cup to wall in a decade, and the yard's best hope before Nate turned up.

records.subject: dessa_kern
records.value: To be the one on the bridge.

records.subject: dessa_kern
records.value: Fast, funny, brutal, and she apologises about an hour later every time.

records.subject: dessa_kern
records.value: Dust comes off a ceiling when she crosses a room, and she watches mouths instead of eyes.

records.subject: dessa_kern
records.value: She would still stand over him during a hold, and hates that about herself.

records.subject: dessa_kern
records.value: Soll has stopped correcting her, which Dessa knows means she is finished growing.

records.subject: dessa_kern_belief
records.value: That Nate is cheating, and that cheating will eventually be found out and punished.

records.subject: dessa_kern_secret
records.value: Her ears never fully came back after her wall, and she reads lips at the far end of a room.

records.subject: oam_barrow
records.value: cast

records.subject: oam_barrow
records.value: The packer who works the city's main gate: a heavy, slow-moving man in a grey layered harness who can end a call by putting a hand on the caller.

records.subject: oam_barrow
records.value: To get Nate packed — a year of layering work and the man will never hear the answer again — because a person who can quiet a wall from outside is the end of the packing house.

records.subject: oam_barrow
records.value: Polite to the point of insult, and never in a hurry, because he never has to be.

records.subject: oam_barrow
records.value: He wades rather than walks, and when he shakes a hand the hand does not close all the way.

records.subject: oam_barrow
records.value: He has offered him a place three times, and the fourth offer will not be an offer.

records.subject: oam_barrow
records.value: He does not know who she used to be; he only knows she is the best teacher in the house.

records.subject: oam_barrow
records.value: He was on the gate the night the quarter came down.

records.subject: oam_barrow_belief
records.value: That the split between the crafts was a decision somebody made, rather than something that happened to one woman.

records.subject: oam_barrow_secret
records.value: He has tried to learn cancelling himself, in a shed, alone, for two years, and cannot do it.

records.subject: wend_ivry
records.value: cast

records.subject: wend_ivry
records.value: An old woman who teaches layering in the packing house under a name that is not hers, and who was, twenty years ago, the last person who could do both.

records.subject: wend_ivry
records.value: To be left alone, and failing that, to make sure the boy who can do both does not end where she ended.

records.subject: wend_ivry
records.value: Dry, amused, gives instructions as if they were gossip.

records.subject: wend_ivry
records.value: She corrects a student's layering with two fingers without looking up, and she flinches at nothing at all, twice a day, out of habit.

records.subject: wend_ivry
records.value: Twice a year, on a bench by the river, and neither of them mentions the quarter.

records.subject: wend_ivry
records.value: She starts by telling him she can hear nothing, which is the first lie she tells him.

records.subject: wend_ivry_belief
records.value: That her sister has never forgiven her.

records.subject: wend_ivry_secret
records.value: She cancelled four streets of stone during a quake to keep them standing and has heard nothing of the answer since — she can still find a beat by eye, from the way dust sits, and tells nobody.

records.subject: tam_orre
records.value: cast

records.subject: tam_orre
records.value: Fourteen, carries the ringing bar, and stands over callers while they hold.

records.subject: tam_orre
records.value: To be a cup-caller before he is sixteen, which everyone in the yard knows is not going to happen.

records.subject: tam_orre
records.value: Talks constantly while nothing is happening and goes completely silent the moment it does.

records.subject: tam_orre
records.value: He stands with the stave low and both feet planted the way he was taught, and he has never once looked at the wall instead of the street.

records.subject: tam_orre
records.value: He has taken two beatings for it and mentioned neither.

records.subject: tam_orre
records.value: Oam has told him the yard will never take him, which is true, and that the house will, which is the hook.

records.subject: tam_orre_belief
records.value: That Nate chose him.

records.subject: tam_orre_secret
records.value: He has already been to the packing house once and been measured for a harness.

records.subject: stack_city
records.value: place

records.subject: stack_city
records.value: A city built up a rock stack in tiers, so every street is somebody else's roof.

records.subject: stack_city
records.value: Nothing here can fall alone. A wall taken on the fourth tier takes three houses on the third, which is why calling inside the city is done at night and quickly.

records.subject: stack_city
records.value: Every conversation on an upper street is held over a hand-sized hole where mortar has walked itself out.

records.subject: stack_city
records.value: On the fourth tier, deliberately, so a failed student's mistake lands on nobody important.

records.subject: stack_city_secret
records.value: The lowest tier is packed straight through from the split, and nobody living knows who did it.

records.subject: the_old_bridge
records.value: place

records.subject: the_old_bridge
records.value: A single stone span across the gorge, older than the split, which no caller has ever brought down.

records.subject: the_old_bridge
records.value: Everything the city eats crosses it, so nobody may try to take it except by permission, and permission has been given eleven times in two centuries.

records.subject: the_old_bridge
records.value: A caller with a hand on the parapet, humming through a whole afternoon, while the fishermen underneath do not even look up.

records.subject: the_old_bridge
records.value: She has been given permission for a twelfth attempt and has one year to use it.

records.subject: the_old_bridge_secret
records.value: It has courses of layered reed and lead inside it, put there before either school existed, which means the split is younger than the bridge and both founding stories are wrong.

records.subject: the_hill_that_answers
records.value: place

records.subject: the_hill_that_answers
records.value: A bare round hill a day's walk out where nothing loose stays put and no animal digs.

records.subject: the_hill_that_answers
records.value: Anyone who sleeps a night on it wakes with their teeth aching and their pack seams opened.

records.subject: the_hill_that_answers
records.value: Boots sink to the ankle in sand that was solid stone a lifetime ago, and a cup of water set down goes still and then does not.

records.subject: the_hill_that_answers
records.value: Whatever it is, it is under the hill and it has not moved in three hundred years.

records.subject: the_hill_that_answers_secret
records.value: Something under it answers at a beat below hearing, and everything within a day's walk is slowly coming apart, which is why the old capital fell.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: institution

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: The walled training ground where callers are made: a bare sand yard with a row of posts, a half-built wall, and a rope bridge over a dry pit.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: The old bridge down, and a hill-caller of its own for the first time in forty years.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: It can put a caller on any gate in the city and can refuse to put one there, which is most of what it actually is.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: Somebody standing over you while you hold, which is the difference between a caller and a dead man.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: Every student is made to take a post while standing under it, and the yard buries the ones who are slow without much ceremony.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: A yard where the sand is always bare of small stones and the shutters on every house facing it are pinned open, because pinned shutters do not rattle.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: She is the yard, and there is no plan for what happens after her.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard
records.value: They take students from the same twelve-year-olds, in the same week, at the same wall.

records.subject: the_shaking_yard_secret
records.value: Soll has already picked who goes on the bridge and has not told the yard, because half of them would leave.

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: institution

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: A long low workshop of grey striped walls where layering is taught and harnesses are fitted, and where the city's gates and treasuries were built.

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: To make the last caller unnecessary.

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: Every gate, every strongroom, and the body of every person in the city who matters.

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: A wall nobody can take, and a body nobody can touch.

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: A year of layering work leaves a person deaf to the answer forever, and everybody who works there has paid it.

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: A smell of wet reed on the wind two streets away, and grey striped combs of insect nest stacked to the ceiling inside.

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: Their students are the ones who failed the other's wall, and both know it.

records.subject: the_packing_house
records.value: He is the hands of it, not the head, and he has begun to notice.

records.subject: the_packing_house_secret
records.value: They cannot pack the old bridge and they never built it, and they have let the city believe otherwise for two hundred years.

records.subject: the_split
records.value: institution

records.subject: the_split
records.value: The generation, two hundred years back, when one craft became two and layering stopped being something a caller did.

records.subject: the_split
records.value: Every wall in the city and every twelve-year-old at the choosing.

records.subject: the_split
records.value: Nobody now living has both, so nobody now living can check whether the split had to happen.

records.subject: the_split
records.value: Two identical lessons taught in two buildings a street apart, each of which calls the other one a fairy story.

records.subject: the_split
records.value: The house was built from the stone of the yard's own outer wall.

records.subject: the_split_belief
records.value: Both schools teach that a body physically cannot hold both, and both cite the same three dead people.

records.subject: the_split_secret
records.value: It was one woman's decision after one bad night, and the old bridge, which is older than the split, has layering inside it.

report.title: The Post-Caller
report.domain: Structural resonance and vibration — the real physics that every solid object has a natural beat set by what it is made of and how big it is, that forcing it at that beat again and again tears it apart while a harder shove out of time does nothing, and that a thing built of mismatched layers has no single beat and cannot be broken this way.
report.inversion_text: One default removed: nothing in this world hunts people. There are no monsters, no beasts to fight, no dungeon. What fills the hole is that the buildings themselves are the danger — a city of stone where any wall can be made to come down, where the ground shifts, where the animals loosen foundations by accident — and every enemy a person has is another person who chose a craft.

world.title: The Post-Caller
world.domain: Structural resonance and vibration — the real physics that every solid object has a natural beat set by what it is made of and how big it is, that forcing it at that beat again and again tears it apart while a harder shove out of time does nothing, and that a thing built of mismatched layers has no single beat and cannot be broken this way.
world.progression_means: How big a thing you can shake to pieces, or hold together against a shake. A caller is named for the largest thing they have taken, and the count runs cup, post, wall, span, hill.
world.inversion: One default removed: nothing in this world hunts people. There are no monsters, no beasts to fight, no dungeon. What fills the hole is that the buildings themselves are the danger — a city of stone where any wall can be made to come down, where the ground shifts, where the animals loosen foundations by accident — and every enemy a person has is another person who chose a craft.
world.premise:
Nate Cairns is twenty-six, has half a physics degree, and spent four years running sound for bands in bars. His one real trick: when a speaker started to howl, he killed the howl by feeding in a second sound shaped to cancel the first.

He is now in a stone city where people take buildings apart by finding the single beat a thing answers to — every solid thing has one — and holding that beat until the thing shakes itself to pieces. They call themselves callers. Against them are the packers, who build in mismatched layers of stone, reed and river mud so a wall answers nothing at all, and who can end a call by laying a hand on the caller doing it. A body is supposed to hold one craft or the other, never both.

Nate holds both, because cancelling is packing done with sound. He can walk up to a wall no caller can touch and hum it dead. It costs him a full day afterward, in which he cannot hear the beat of anything and is an ordinary man, and both schools know it.

Callers are named for the biggest thing they can bring down: cup, post, wall, span, hill. Nate is a post. The yard that trains him wants the old bridge, which no caller has ever taken.

protagonist.edge: He sets his palm on a packed wall that has beaten three callers, hums a note under the one it is already carrying, and the wall goes dead in his hand — the dust that was climbing it drops straight down, and the room goes so quiet people check their own ears.
protagonist.wants: To get to hill, where a caller drops a cliff face and holds a whole town's stone through the ground moving, and to find out who or what pulled him here, because something reached for a beat that does not exist in this world and he came along it.
protagonist.price: For a full day after a cancel he hears nothing of the answer — plain hands, plain ears, a man anyone can walk up behind. Packers count it as theft of their craft and want him quieted; callers count it as cheating and will not stand over him while he holds.

systems.name: Calling
systems.logic: Every solid thing answers at one beat, set by what it is made of and how big it is. Push in time with that beat and each push adds to the last until the thing tears itself apart. Push harder but out of time and nothing happens at all. So the craft is not strength, it is patience and accuracy: find the beat, then hold it while the world tries to stop you.
systems.manifests_as: A caller stands with a flat palm on a gate, humming one low note, and after a minute the hinges begin to knock back at her in time.
systems.interface: On open ground and at any distance the caller wins: a packer must be within arm's reach to do anything, and a wall-caller can drop a gate from across a yard. Inside anything a packer built, the packer wins absolutely — a packed wall answers nothing and no caller of any name has ever taken one. Hand to hand, the packer wins: a hand laid flat on a calling caller kills the note dead. Children are made to choose at twelve, at the yard's wall, and the choice is physical rather than sworn — a year of packing work leaves a body unable to hear the answer ever again, and no one has come back from it. What a caller can do that a packer never can is take a thing down from far away. What a packer can do that a caller never can is make a thing that cannot be taken at all.
systems.hidden_personality: The answer is indifferent. It has no side and takes no notice of who is holding the beat, which is why the old bridge has beaten everybody who ever tried.
systems.view_withholds: Nothing tells a caller what a thing answers at. You find it by hand, by ear, by wasting an afternoon.

criterion.evaluates: The largest thing this person has brought down in front of witnesses, and the largest thing they have held together against a shake.

ranks.visible_form: Water in a glass beside them shivers when they breathe. They keep the first cup they ever cracked on their belt, in three pieces on a wire.
ranks.cost_to_reach: A season of standing with a hand on things until they answer, and everything breakable they own is broken by the end of it. The hand they learn with goes clumsy for months and they eat left-handed in front of everybody.
ranks.grants: Bring apart anything they can close a hand around: snap the pin in a lock, split a stone, crack ice, take the ring off a seized bolt. It works through a door if they can touch the door.

ranks.visible_form: Doors rattle in their frames as they walk past, and shopkeepers put a hand on their shutters when they come up the street.
ranks.cost_to_reach: They must take down a roof post while standing under it, with the yard watching, and not step out. Some do not step out fast enough.
ranks.grants: Bring down anything one person could carry or lean on — a door, a cart axle, a spear in a man's hands, a ladder under a climber — from a few paces away, and take a good half-minute doing it.

ranks.visible_form: Dust falls out of a ceiling when they walk under it, and the sand in the street is smooth and stoneless wherever they have stood a while.
ranks.cost_to_reach: They stand inside the shadow of the wall they are taking until it goes. Everyone who does it comes out with their ears ringing so hard they hear nothing at all for three days, and in those three days anybody at all can come up behind them.
ranks.grants: Drop a house wall or a gate from across a yard, and hold a wall standing through a shake that should have laid it flat.

ranks.visible_form: Birds leave a roof before they get to it. Horses will not stand still under them.
ranks.cost_to_reach: The yard puts their own teacher out on the span and makes them take it. Whoever is on the bridge remembers it, and half of them never speak to the caller again.
ranks.grants: Take a bridge out from under a marching column, or hold one up while their own people cross it, from far enough away that nobody can reach them in time.

ranks.visible_form: Glass rings when they enter a room. Sleeping people wake as they pass the bed. The ground around them is always bare of small stones, because everything loose has walked itself away.
ranks.cost_to_reach: After it, nothing fine near them is ever quiet again. They cannot sit with anyone frail, cannot hold a newborn, cannot sleep in a house with anybody else in it. And the packing house stops trying to recruit them and starts trying to pack them.
ranks.grants: Bring a cliff face down into a valley, hold a whole town's stone together while the ground moves under it, and — because a living body has a beat too, if you can hold it — stop a man dead where he stands, across a field, without touching him.

rules.rule: Every solid thing answers at one beat, set by what it is made of and how big it is. Find it, push in time, and the thing comes apart. Push out of time, however hard, and nothing happens.
rules.manifests_as: He lays his hand flat on a cart axle and hums until the hum comes back at him louder than he made it, and the axle jumps out of its bed.

consequences.consequence: Nobody builds anything to one size any more. Good stonework runs in courses of different thicknesses on purpose, and a mason who cuts a hundred matching blocks is laughed out of the yard.
Armies never march in step. Officers set an uneven count on purpose, and a column that falls into a rhythm crossing a bridge is stopped and shouted at.
Children are taught which rooms not to sing in. Stone stairwells and cellar arches are quiet places by custom, and a man humming in one gets stared at the way a man striking matches in a barn does.

rules.rule: Nothing goes on the first push. The beat has to be held while the thing takes it, and the bigger the thing the longer the hold. A caller in the middle of a hold cannot do anything else, cannot move much, and cannot defend themselves.
rules.manifests_as: She kneels with both hands on the gate and a boy stands over her with a stave, watching the street, while she counts through her teeth.

consequences.consequence: House-breakers keep a cup-caller for locks and a second body to stand over them, so burglary is a two-person trade and locks are now made of two metals fitted together so they answer at nothing.
To buy one caller a full minute on a gate an army spends bodies in front of her, and every siege plan is really a plan about a minute.
The long hold has become a prayer. Their word for patience and their word for the hold are the same word, and mourners sit with a hand on a stone for as long as the dead person's age in breaths.

rules.rule: A living body has a beat like anything else, but it moves — every breath and every heartbeat shifts it — so it cannot be held long enough to matter unless the caller is at hill.
rules.manifests_as: A guard walking a nervous street breathes deliberately raggedly and hums flat and tuneless, the way people whistle in the dark.

consequences.consequence: Frightened people breathe on purpose out of rhythm, and a man doing it in a market is a man who thinks somebody is after him, which everyone can see.
Bodyguards are trained to hum tunelessly and constantly around whoever they are guarding, so no note near them ever settles, and a quiet bodyguard is a bribed one.
No ordinary men can hold a hill-caller, so cities keep packers on their gates instead of soldiers, and the packing house has quietly become the thing that decides who walks in.

systems.name: Packing
systems.logic: A thing made of mismatched layers has no single beat. The push spreads out through stone, reed, mud and lead thread, each of which answers at something different, and it dies before it can add to itself. So the packers do not fight a call, they make a thing that cannot be called. Their whole craft is layering, and their creed is that anything with one clean beat is a thing already waiting to fall down.
systems.manifests_as: A grey striped wall, ugly as a wasp's nest, with reed ends and river mud showing between the courses — and a caller standing in front of it for an hour with nothing at all happening.
systems.interface: See the calling side of it: distance and open ground go to the caller, arm's reach and packed ground go to the packer, and no body has ever held both crafts.
systems.hidden_personality: The packing house believes it is the only reason the city is still standing, and it is not entirely wrong.
systems.view_withholds: From the outside there is no way to tell a packed wall from a plain one until a caller has already wasted an hour on it. Packers like it that way.

criterion.evaluates: Whether a thing answers at all. There is no scale here: a wall is either dead or it is not, and a wall that is half packed is a wall.

rules.rule: Build a thing in alternating layers of unlike stuff — stone, reed, mud, lead thread — and it answers at no single beat. No caller of any name can take it.
rules.manifests_as: A packer thumbs a wet reed mat down between two stone courses, slaps mud over it, and says nothing while the caller she beat that morning watches from the road.

consequences.consequence: Packed houses are hot, dark and thick-walled, and every home in the city smells faintly of wet reed. Anyone who grew up poor grew up in that smell and knows a packed room by nose in the dark.
A packed gate cannot be called down, so sieges are back to ladders, fire and starving people out, and a war now takes a season instead of an afternoon.
Anything worth stealing lives in a packed room, so thieves have stopped calling locks and started digging under floors, and the city's cellars are full of holes nobody admits to.

rules.rule: A person can be packed too: a layered harness of hide, reed and lead thread worn under the clothes for months until the body under it answers at nothing. While it is on, no caller can touch them.
rules.manifests_as: He unbuttons his coat to show the grey mat underneath, and when he reaches out to shake a hand the hand does not close properly.

consequences.consequence: Every ruler in the city wears one, so every ruler in the city is visibly slow, and the way you spot power in a crowd is by who moves like a man wading.
A packed man cannot feel a fever in his own child's forehead and cannot swim in the river, so the wealthy do not go near water and their children are checked by servants.
The front rank of any column is packed men who cannot run, which is why a charge in this city walks.

cast.is_a: Twenty-six, half a physics degree, four years running sound in bars, and now a post-caller in a city he cannot find on any map.
cast.wants: To get to hill, and to know what reached for him.
cast.secret: He has already tried to cancel a person and it worked for a second and a half, and he has told nobody.
cast.false_belief: That because both crafts come easy to him, one of the two schools will eventually decide he is worth protecting.
cast.voice_tag: Talks like a man explaining a mixing desk to somebody who did not ask: short, flat, one joke too many when he is frightened.
cast.manifests_as: He listens to a room before he looks at it, and he taps things — tables, walls, his own cup — without noticing he does it.

relationships.note: She took him in because he could find a beat in one afternoon, and she has not told him what she wants him for.
She got to wall the hard way, standing in the shadow of it, and he skipped every step she bled for.
Oam saw him cancel a wall and understood immediately what it means for the packing house.
The boy stands over him while he holds, carries the bar, and has never once run.

cast.is_a: A span-caller who runs the yard where callers are trained, and the only person alive who has taken a bridge with somebody standing on it.
cast.wants: The old bridge down before she dies, because she has been told her whole life it cannot be done.
cast.secret: Her older sister is alive, teaches in the packing house under another name, and Soll goes to see her twice a year.
cast.false_belief: That the bridge has beaten callers because none of them were strong enough.
cast.voice_tag: Short sentences, never raises her voice, ends instructions with the price of getting them wrong.
cast.manifests_as: Birds go off a roof before she reaches it, and the horse at the yard gate will not stand still while she talks.

relationships.note: She has already decided he is the one who takes the bridge, and has not said so.
She was the one who fetched the packers the night Wend went silent.
He was at the gate that night and did nothing, which is not quite true.

cast.is_a: Nineteen, the fastest anyone has gone from cup to wall in a decade, and the yard's best hope before Nate turned up.
cast.wants: To be the one on the bridge.
cast.secret: Her ears never fully came back after her wall, and she reads lips at the far end of a room.
cast.false_belief: That Nate is cheating, and that cheating will eventually be found out and punished.
cast.voice_tag: Fast, funny, brutal, and she apologises about an hour later every time.
cast.manifests_as: Dust comes off a ceiling when she crosses a room, and she watches mouths instead of eyes.

relationships.note: She would still stand over him during a hold, and hates that about herself.
Soll has stopped correcting her, which Dessa knows means she is finished growing.

cast.is_a: The packer who works the city's main gate: a heavy, slow-moving man in a grey layered harness who can end a call by putting a hand on the caller.
cast.wants: To get Nate packed — a year of layering work and the man will never hear the answer again — because a person who can quiet a wall from outside is the end of the packing house.
cast.secret: He has tried to learn cancelling himself, in a shed, alone, for two years, and cannot do it.
cast.false_belief: That the split between the crafts was a decision somebody made, rather than something that happened to one woman.
cast.voice_tag: Polite to the point of insult, and never in a hurry, because he never has to be.
cast.manifests_as: He wades rather than walks, and when he shakes a hand the hand does not close all the way.

relationships.note: He has offered him a place three times, and the fourth offer will not be an offer.
He does not know who she used to be; he only knows she is the best teacher in the house.
He was on the gate the night the quarter came down.

cast.is_a: An old woman who teaches layering in the packing house under a name that is not hers, and who was, twenty years ago, the last person who could do both.
cast.wants: To be left alone, and failing that, to make sure the boy who can do both does not end where she ended.
cast.secret: She cancelled four streets of stone during a quake to keep them standing and has heard nothing of the answer since — she can still find a beat by eye, from the way dust sits, and tells nobody.
cast.false_belief: That her sister has never forgiven her.
cast.voice_tag: Dry, amused, gives instructions as if they were gossip.
cast.manifests_as: She corrects a student's layering with two fingers without looking up, and she flinches at nothing at all, twice a day, out of habit.

relationships.note: Twice a year, on a bench by the river, and neither of them mentions the quarter.
She starts by telling him she can hear nothing, which is the first lie she tells him.

cast.is_a: Fourteen, carries the ringing bar, and stands over callers while they hold.
cast.wants: To be a cup-caller before he is sixteen, which everyone in the yard knows is not going to happen.
cast.secret: He has already been to the packing house once and been measured for a harness.
cast.voice_tag: Talks constantly while nothing is happening and goes completely silent the moment it does.
cast.manifests_as: He stands with the stave low and both feet planted the way he was taught, and he has never once looked at the wall instead of the street.

Oam has told him the yard will never take him, which is true, and that the house will, which is the hook.

institutions.is_a: The walled training ground where callers are made: a bare sand yard with a row of posts, a half-built wall, and a rope bridge over a dry pit.
institutions.wants: The old bridge down, and a hill-caller of its own for the first time in forty years.
institutions.reach: It can put a caller on any gate in the city and can refuse to put one there, which is most of what it actually is.
institutions.grants: Somebody standing over you while you hold, which is the difference between a caller and a dead man.
institutions.prices_the_present: Every student is made to take a post while standing under it, and the yard buries the ones who are slow without much ceremony.
institutions.manifests_as: A yard where the sand is always bare of small stones and the shutters on every house facing it are pinned open, because pinned shutters do not rattle.
institutions.secret: Soll has already picked who goes on the bridge and has not told the yard, because half of them would leave.

relationships.note: She is the yard, and there is no plan for what happens after her.
They take students from the same twelve-year-olds, in the same week, at the same wall.

institutions.is_a: A long low workshop of grey striped walls where layering is taught and harnesses are fitted, and where the city's gates and treasuries were built.
institutions.wants: To make the last caller unnecessary.
institutions.reach: Every gate, every strongroom, and the body of every person in the city who matters.
institutions.grants: A wall nobody can take, and a body nobody can touch.
institutions.prices_the_present: A year of layering work leaves a person deaf to the answer forever, and everybody who works there has paid it.
institutions.manifests_as: A smell of wet reed on the wind two streets away, and grey striped combs of insect nest stacked to the ceiling inside.
institutions.secret: They cannot pack the old bridge and they never built it, and they have let the city believe otherwise for two hundred years.

relationships.note: Their students are the ones who failed the other's wall, and both know it.
He is the hands of it, not the head, and he has begun to notice.

places.is_a: A city built up a rock stack in tiers, so every street is somebody else's roof.
places.manifests_as: Every conversation on an upper street is held over a hand-sized hole where mortar has walked itself out.
places.prices_the_present: Nothing here can fall alone. A wall taken on the fourth tier takes three houses on the third, which is why calling inside the city is done at night and quickly.
places.secret: The lowest tier is packed straight through from the split, and nobody living knows who did it.

relationships.note: On the fourth tier, deliberately, so a failed student's mistake lands on nobody important.

places.is_a: A single stone span across the gorge, older than the split, which no caller has ever brought down.
places.manifests_as: A caller with a hand on the parapet, humming through a whole afternoon, while the fishermen underneath do not even look up.
places.prices_the_present: Everything the city eats crosses it, so nobody may try to take it except by permission, and permission has been given eleven times in two centuries.
places.secret: It has courses of layered reed and lead inside it, put there before either school existed, which means the split is younger than the bridge and both founding stories are wrong.

relationships.note: She has been given permission for a twelfth attempt and has one year to use it.

places.is_a: A bare round hill a day's walk out where nothing loose stays put and no animal digs.
places.manifests_as: Boots sink to the ankle in sand that was solid stone a lifetime ago, and a cup of water set down goes still and then does not.
places.prices_the_present: Anyone who sleeps a night on it wakes with their teeth aching and their pack seams opened.
places.secret: Something under it answers at a beat below hearing, and everything within a day's walk is slowly coming apart, which is why the old capital fell.

relationships.note: Whatever it is, it is under the hill and it has not moved in three hundred years.

agencies.is_a: A beat coming out of the ground under the hill, too low for any ear, that never stops.
agencies.wants: Nothing. It is not a person and has never been one.
agencies.recognises: Anybody who calls within a day's walk of it, whose note it takes up and continues after they stop.
agencies.reach: A day's walk in every direction, and further in bad weather.
agencies.grants: A caller working near it never has to hold — the beat is held for them — and can take something four names above their own.
agencies.prices_the_present: Everything they take stays taking. A wall dropped near the hill goes on coming apart for weeks, and so does the house behind it, and so does the road.
agencies.false_belief: Everyone believes it is the ruin of the old capital settling.
agencies.manifests_as: He stops humming and the wall keeps going anyway, faster, and he cannot make it stop.
agencies.secret: It is getting louder, at about the rate a man's hair goes grey, and stack city is inside the edge of it now.

relationships.note: Nobody has dug down to find out, because digging there is how the last three parties died.

carriers.is_a: A forearm of soft iron that holds a found beat for about a day.
carriers.grants: Anybody at all can use a beat somebody else found, which is how a cup-caller opens a strongroom lock a wall-caller found for them.
carriers.manifests_as: A warm bar in a boy's satchel that faintly hums against his ribs all afternoon and goes cold and quiet the moment it is spent.
carriers.prices_the_present: Whoever put the beat in cannot call anything until it is used up, so a crew that carries bars is a crew with one member deliberately made useless.
carriers.secret: A bar that has held a beat too long takes a second one badly, and three of the yard's bars are already lying about what they hold.

relationships.note: He has never dropped one, and he has been offered money for one twice.

history.is_a: The generation, two hundred years back, when one craft became two and layering stopped being something a caller did.
history.reach: Every wall in the city and every twelve-year-old at the choosing.
history.prices_the_present: Nobody now living has both, so nobody now living can check whether the split had to happen.
history.false_belief: Both schools teach that a body physically cannot hold both, and both cite the same three dead people.
history.manifests_as: Two identical lessons taught in two buildings a street apart, each of which calls the other one a fairy story.
history.secret: It was one woman's decision after one bad night, and the old bridge, which is older than the split, has layering inside it.

relationships.note: The house was built from the stone of the yard's own outer wall.

creatures.is_a: Badger-sized burrowing animals that drum with their foreheads to loosen packed earth.
creatures.mechanism: They drum faster and faster until the soil around them starts answering, and then it turns to loose sand and they simply swim through it.
creatures.ecology: They follow old stone, because worked foundations are the easiest digging in the country, so every city in the world has them under it.
creatures.human_use: Callers keep one in a box: hold it against a wall and its drumming settles on whatever that wall answers at, and a caller who cannot find a beat in an afternoon rents one for the morning.
creatures.behaviour: Terrified of people, blind in daylight, and they will collapse a cellar without ever knowing anybody lived above it.
creatures.manifests_as: A fine sifting of sand out of a cellar wall, and a knocking under the floor that speeds up whenever anybody in the room talks.

creatures.is_a: Reed-nesting insects the size of a thumb that build in alternating layers of mud, chewed reed and their own shed hair.
creatures.mechanism: Nothing they build answers at any single beat, because no two layers of it are the same stuff.
creatures.ecology: They nest under eaves along the river and cannot survive anywhere the reeds do not grow.
creatures.human_use: The packing house farms them and lines the inside of walls with their broken-up combs, which is why a packed room smells of wet reed.
creatures.behaviour: They sting once, badly, and only if you take a comb while the sun is on it.
creatures.manifests_as: Grey striped combs under every eave in the lower city, and a boy on a ladder at dawn cutting them down into a sack.

creatures.is_a: Black birds that will nest only in packed walls.
creatures.mechanism: A plain wall shivers all night from carts and wind and shakes them awake; a packed wall does not move at all.
creatures.ecology: They have followed the packing house's work across the whole city in two hundred years and are now found nowhere else.
creatures.human_use: A thief looking for the strongroom looks for the crows, and the house has spent forty years trying to poison them off its own roofs.
creatures.behaviour: Loud, unafraid, and they scream when a wall they are sitting on starts to answer, which has saved more lives than the yard likes to admit.
creatures.manifests_as: Six black birds going up off a gatehouse all at once, half a breath before anybody feels anything.

bonds.joint_ability: She can still tell what a thing answers at by eye, from how dust sits on it, and he can kill a beat he has been handed — so between them they can quiet something neither could touch alone, without either of them ever putting a hand on it.
bonds.trait_link: Both of them can do the thing the city has agreed is impossible, and both of them have learned to do it where nobody is looking.

mysteries.question: Why has the old bridge beaten every caller who has ever tried to take it?
mysteries.answer: It has layered courses of reed and lead buried inside the stone, put there before either school existed. It was packed — which means the split is younger than the bridge, and both schools' stories about how the crafts divided are wrong.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Soll Ivry, who believes it has beaten everybody because nobody has yet been strong enough, and who is training Nate on that belief.

mysteries.question: Who was the last person who could do both, and what happened to her?
mysteries.answer: Wend Ivry, Soll's older sister. She cancelled four streets of stone during a quake to hold them up, and has heard nothing of the answer since. She is alive, teaching layering in the packing house under another name, and she can still read a beat off the way dust sits.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: The packing house, which believes she is a gifted old teacher with no past worth asking about.

mysteries.question: Why does nothing dig on the bare hill, and why is everything within a day's walk of it slowly falling apart?
mysteries.answer: Something under the hill answers at a beat below hearing and has been doing it for centuries. It is what brought down the old capital, it takes up any note called near it and keeps going after the caller stops, and its edge has now reached stack city.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Everyone, who calls it the ruin of the old capital settling.

mysteries.question: How did Nate get here?
mysteries.answer: A caller reaching for the beat of something that does not exist in this world found a note that answered from outside it and pulled him along it. She is alive, she has been listening for him ever since, and she wants him back because he is the only proof her method worked.

directives.text: Fast, plain, popcorn prose. Never explain how any of it works — show a hand on a wall, a count through the teeth, a price paid.

No technical vocabulary from the real physics ever reaches the page. Nobody says frequency, resonance, amplitude, damping, phase or interference. The page's words are beat, answer, hold, push, pack, dead, quiet.
No debts, no registers, no filed papers, no courts. Every price is paid in a body, in time, in risk, in something a person can no longer do, or in somebody who is now against them.
The first twelve scenes take Nate from cancelling a wall in front of the wrong witness to standing on the old bridge with a hand on the parapet, and settle the bridge's secret on the way.
End chapters on a price becoming visible rather than on a threat being announced.

candidates.title: The Cold Hour
candidates.premise:
Ilen Coble is twenty-two and grew up in a fishing town on the coast, where the sea stays warm after dark and the wind turns around at night.

Inland, on the high dry plain, everyone knows the sky only works by day: the sun heats the ground, warm air climbs, and the water in it comes out as haze, cloud and rain. After sundown nothing climbs, so the people who move weather — drawers, they call themselves — stop at dark. Ilen never learned that, because on his coast it is false. At night, on wet ground, he can pull fog thick enough to hide a road.

Drawers are named for how much of the day they can work. Lowest is the cold hour before dawn, when all you can do is pull drinking water out of dry air. Then the climb. Then the overturn, where a man puts a cloud over a dry field at noon and drops a wind out of it that knocks a rider flat. Highest is kept weather, which one woman on the plain has: she can bring rain to country that has none, and has not been warm in nine years, because a drawer cannot make heat, only move it, and it comes out of him.

By day Ilen is at the climb, second of the four, and the worst in his year. The plain has been dry for three years, and he thinks the farmers in the green valley below did it without meaning to.

records.value: Warm air holds water and cold air cannot. The sun heats the ground, the ground heats the air on it, that air climbs, and as it climbs it cools and lets go of its water as haze, then cloud, then rain. A drawer does not make any of that; a drawer moves heat from where it is to where it is wanted, and starts a lift that then runs on its own. So everything they do is a matter of when — the sky has to already be halfway to doing it.

records.subject: sys_drawing
records.value: Over a holder's valley a drawer can do nothing at all. The ground there is shaded, wet and cool, it never gets hot, and air that will not warm will not rise no matter who is standing on it — the refusal is the landscape's, and no amount of talent gets past it. Out on the burnt plain the holders are equally helpless: a drawer can lay hail across a season's work in an afternoon and there is no answer to it. So the whole war is about ground — who gets to keep it green and who gets to keep it bare. A body cannot hold both crafts: a drawer is trained by thirst until they can feel damp in the air, and a holder's hands are in water every day of their life and go dead to it by about fifteen. Children choose at twelve, on the burnt plain, in front of both houses. What a holder can do that no drawer ever can is keep a town alive through a drought, because you cannot make rain out of dry air. What a drawer can do that no holder ever can is end a siege in one afternoon.

records.value: On a lid day the best drawer in the world is a wrapped-up person sitting by a fire, and everybody's temper is short.

records.subject: the_lid
records.value: Two hours of nothing, and then the whole sky standing up in one white tower while the person who started it walks backwards away from it.

records.subject: the_lid
records.value: It has barely lifted since the shade line was finished.

records.subject: the_lid_belief
records.value: Students believe the lid is something a strong enough drawer can push through.

records.subject: the_lid_secret
records.value: A lid over the plain has held for most of three years, which is not weather, and Tay has half worked out why.

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: cast

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: Twenty-two, from a fishing town on the coast, first year at the plain school and last in it.

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: Kept weather, and rain back on the plain.

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: Talks like somebody explaining the tide to a person who has never seen the sea — patient, over-detailed, and slightly too pleased about it.

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: He looks at the sky before he looks at whoever is speaking to him, and he is always awake at the wrong hours.

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: She has not thrown him out, which everyone in the year has an opinion about.

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: Rusk is at the overturn and cannot lose to him by daylight, which is exactly the problem.

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: She is the only person who has watched him work at night and not immediately told somebody.

records.subject: ilen_coble
records.value: She still runs the family boat and writes to him about the wind, which is the only reason he knows the coast's night turn is holding.

records.subject: ilen_coble_belief
records.value: That if he shows the school what he can do at night, they will change what they teach.

records.subject: ilen_coble_secret
records.value: He has already fogged a night camp on the plain once, on his own, for no reason but to see if he could, and forty men wandered off a road because of it.

records.subject: master_tay
records.value: cast

records.subject: master_tay
records.value: The only drawer alive at kept weather, who runs the school on the burnt plain and has not been warm in nine years.

records.subject: master_tay
records.value: To find someone who can carry kept weather after her, because both of the two before her walked into the sea.

records.subject: master_tay
records.value: Very quiet, very short, and she says the price of a thing before she says what it does.

records.subject: master_tay
records.value: Frost on the inside of the shutters of a room she has been sitting in, and two fires burning in her quarters in high summer.

records.subject: master_tay
records.value: She kept him because she wants to know what the coast knows, and has told him none of that.

records.subject: master_tay
records.value: He is the school's obvious heir and she has never once said so.

records.subject: master_tay
records.value: They have her teacher, they have been kind to him for eleven years, and she cannot get to him.

records.subject: master_tay_belief
records.value: That the drought on the plain is the sky's doing and will turn on its own if she outlasts it.

records.subject: master_tay_secret
records.value: Her own teacher is alive and being kept comfortable in the green valley, where no weather she can make will ever reach him.

records.subject: rusk_delane
records.value: cast

records.subject: rusk_delane
records.value: Twenty-four, at the overturn, first in his year and the best any of them have seen since Tay herself.

records.subject: rusk_delane
records.value: To be the one who ends the drought in front of everybody.

records.subject: rusk_delane
records.value: Generous in public, exact in private, and he remembers every number anybody has ever posted.

records.subject: rusk_delane
records.value: Kites turning over him within the hour, wherever he is standing, and the whole school looking up.

records.subject: rusk_delane
records.value: He has offered twice to train him mornings, which was meant kindly and landed as charity.

records.subject: rusk_delane
records.value: He has waited four years for her to say it and she has not.

records.subject: rusk_delane
records.value: Brask has already paid for his winter, which the school does not know.

records.subject: rusk_delane_belief
records.value: That Ilen's night work is a trick with damp ground and will be exposed the first time it matters.

records.subject: rusk_delane_secret
records.value: He reached the overturn on a day the lid broke on its own, and he knows it, and he has never repeated it cleanly.

records.subject: pell_orrow
records.value: cast

records.subject: pell_orrow
records.value: Nineteen, a holder from the green valley, whose hands have been in water every day since she was eight.

records.subject: pell_orrow
records.value: To finish her grandmother's terrace line without breaking the house's rule that nothing may be gained at anybody's cost.

records.subject: pell_orrow
records.value: Says less than she knows, and answers questions about three seconds late.

records.subject: pell_orrow
records.value: White wrinkled fingers at midday and a blind eel going back into its hole.

records.subject: pell_orrow
records.value: Night, wet valley ground: the one place and hour where a drawer and a holder are not in each other's way.

records.subject: pell_orrow
records.value: Her family have kept the upper springs for six generations and she is the one they expect to keep them next.

records.subject: pell_orrow
records.value: For forty miles of shade planted by people who meant nothing but good by it.

records.subject: pell_orrow_belief
records.value: That she can put it right quietly, on her own, before anybody upstream notices.

records.subject: pell_orrow_secret
records.value: She worked out two years ago that the valley's shade is what killed the plain's weather, and has said it to nobody because the house's whole rule depends on it not being true.

records.subject: captain_brask
records.value: cast

records.subject: captain_brask
records.value: A soldier who has been trying for two years to get a drawer of his own for a siege that a wet valley keeps winning.

records.subject: captain_brask
records.value: An overturn dropped on a valley in one afternoon, and he does not care which house's valley it is.

records.subject: captain_brask
records.value: Cheerful, direct, buys the drinks, and asks the same question four different ways.

records.subject: captain_brask
records.value: He turns up at the school on lid days, when he knows nobody will be out working.

records.subject: captain_brask
records.value: Paid for his winter and expects an afternoon's work for it.

records.subject: captain_brask
records.value: Twice, in front of witnesses, and he has been polite about it both times.

records.subject: captain_brask_belief
records.value: That weather is a weapon like any other and can be aimed.

records.subject: captain_brask_secret
records.value: He has already been told by Tay that hail on a valley is the one thing she will not do, and he has stopped asking her.

records.subject: sura_coble
records.value: cast

records.subject: sura_coble
records.value: Ilen's older sister, who runs the family boat out of the coast town and has never been more than a day inland.

records.subject: sura_coble
records.value: Him home, or at least him useful.

records.subject: sura_coble
records.value: Writes the way she talks: weather first, family second, nothing about herself.

records.subject: sura_coble
records.value: A folded letter that starts with which way the wind came round on which night.

records.subject: sura_coble
records.value: Her letters are the only record anybody has of a night turn, and neither of them knows that yet.

records.subject: sura_coble_belief
records.value: That the school is a place that will look after him.

records.subject: sura_coble_secret
records.value: The night wind on their stretch of coast has shifted in the last two years and she has not told him, because he would come back.

records.subject: the_burnt_plain
records.value: place

records.subject: the_burnt_plain
records.value: A high flat of ash-coloured stone and dead grass where the school stands and where children choose at twelve.

records.subject: the_burnt_plain
records.value: Nothing grows here now, so everything the school eats comes up the valley road, and the valley knows it.

records.subject: the_burnt_plain
records.value: Knees skinned through the cloth by the second week, and dust devils walking about on their own all afternoon.

records.subject: the_burnt_plain
records.value: Built here because it is the only ground that still lifts.

records.subject: the_burnt_plain_secret
