records.subject: the_green_valley
records.value: place

records.subject: the_green_valley
records.value: A shaded terraced valley below the plain, green in the third year of a drought, forty miles long.

records.subject: the_green_valley
records.value: A drawer standing in it can do nothing at all, and knows it within about ten minutes.

records.subject: the_green_valley
records.value: You come over the lip out of white glare into cold air under trees, and everybody who does it stops walking.

records.subject: the_green_valley
records.value: Six generations, and the shade line is still forty years from finished.

records.subject: the_green_valley_secret
records.value: Its shade is the reason the plain above it has no weather.

records.subject: saltmouth
records.value: place

records.subject: saltmouth
records.value: The coast town Ilen comes from: boats, wet flats, and a wind that turns around every night.

records.subject: saltmouth
records.value: Nobody there has ever thought it was worth mentioning, so no drawer inland has ever heard of it.

records.subject: saltmouth
records.value: Fog standing over the water at midnight on a still, clear night, every night, for nothing.

records.subject: saltmouth
records.value: He has not been back in a year and has stopped saying when he will.

records.subject: saltmouth_secret
records.value: The night turn there has been weakening for two years, and Sura has not written it down.

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: institution

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: A low stone compound on the burnt plain where drawers are trained, with a bare stamped field, a well nobody uses, and shutters that close at dusk.

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: An heir to kept weather before Tay stops.

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: It can send a drawer to any town on the plain, and every town on the plain wants one and can be refused.

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: Somebody to warm you and carry you after you have spent yourself, which nobody working alone has.

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: First-year students spend a season being given one cup a day, and about a fifth of them go home.

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: A horn at dusk, and forty people stopping mid-stride and walking in.

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: Same twelve-year-olds, same week, same patch of burnt ground.

records.subject: the_plain_school
records.value: There is no plan for the day after her.

records.subject: the_plain_school_secret
records.value: They have known for six years that the drought started the same season the valley finished its long shade line, and the master has not said it out loud because saying it starts a war.

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: institution

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: The family and the households who keep the green valley's springs — terraces, shade trees, packed channels, and six generations of hands in cold water.

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: To finish the shade line to the valley's head, which will take another thirty years and which they consider the work of their lives.

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: The valley, everyone who has ever walked into it in a dry year, and the water of four towns downstream.

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: Green ground in the third year of a drought, and a place no weather can reach.

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: Their children are in water from eight years old and are deaf to the air by fifteen, and none of them can ever be drawers.

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: A green valley you can see from twenty miles out on a plain the colour of ash.

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: The one house each considers the reason the other exists.

records.subject: the_valley_house
records.value: They have been keeping her old teacher comfortable for eleven years and consider it a kindness.

records.subject: the_valley_house_secret
records.value: Their shade line is what killed the plain's lift. They do not know it, they did not mean it, and by their own rule the work would have to be undone.

records.subject: the_founders_night
records.value: institution

records.subject: the_founders_night
records.value: The night, eighty years back, when a coastal drawer fogged the burnt plain in the dark and nearly killed the school's founder in the confusion.

records.subject: the_founders_night
records.value: Every student who has ever been told to stop work at dusk.

records.subject: the_founders_night
records.value: No coastal student has been taken since, and the rule against night work is taught as physics rather than as a grudge.

records.subject: the_founders_night
records.value: A horn at dusk and a master who will not explain why the horn exists.

records.subject: the_founders_night
records.value: It is the oldest rule in the place and the only one nobody may ask about.

records.subject: the_founders_night_belief
records.value: Everyone at the school believes the dusk rule was written because nothing can be done at night.

records.subject: the_founders_night_secret
records.value: The founder wrote the rule knowing full well the coast is an exception, and wrote it anyway.

records.subject: kites
records.value: creature

records.subject: kites
records.value: Great sailing birds, wider than a man is tall, that cannot flap far and so can only fly where air is climbing.

records.subject: kites
records.value: Eleven birds turning in a slow wheel over a bare hill, all the same way round, and a boy on a wall counting them out loud.

records.subject: kites
records.value: They hang inside a rising column and are carried up it, then glide out and look for the next one, all day, without a wingbeat.

records.subject: kites
records.value: They circle over bare hot ground and never once over the green valley, and their range has shrunk with the plain's lift for three years running.

records.subject: kites
records.value: Drawers read them. Where kites are turning, the sky will work; first-years are sent up a hill at dawn to watch and count them, and a drawer who is working well can be found from miles away by the wheel of birds over him.

records.subject: kites
records.value: Utterly indifferent to people, and they will land beside a drawer who holds a column open, close enough to touch, for as long as it stays open.

records.subject: kites
records.value: A drawer at the overturn can hold a column open where they choose and put kites there, which is how a signal is sent across a plain in an afternoon.

records.subject: stormflies
records.value: creature

records.subject: stormflies
records.value: Black flies the size of a grain that hatch in the hours before rain.

records.subject: stormflies
records.value: A black smear crawling along a road at ankle height, and every window on the street banging shut behind it.

records.subject: stormflies
records.value: They come out of the ground when the air goes light and thin, which happens ahead of weather.

records.subject: stormflies
records.value: They lie in the soil for years and hatch on the plain perhaps twice a year now, where it used to be twenty.

records.subject: stormflies
records.value: Everybody's warning. A black smear along the ground means shutters closed and washing in by evening, and the plain's children are paid a coin a cup for them.

records.subject: stormflies
records.value: They get into the eyes and the mouth and they do not bite, which is somehow worse.

records.subject: well_eels
records.value: creature

records.subject: well_eels
records.value: Blind white eels, arm-long, that live in the water under the valley.

records.subject: well_eels
records.value: A girl with her arm in a hole to the shoulder, drawing out something long and white, looking at it, and putting it back.

records.subject: well_eels
records.value: They cannot survive in moving water and die within a day if the ground water starts to run.

records.subject: well_eels
records.value: They exist only under worked valleys and have followed the holders' terracing for six generations.

records.subject: well_eels
records.value: Holders read them: a hole with a fat eel in it is water that has been standing quietly for years, and a hole with none is a warning that something upstream has been cut.

records.subject: well_eels
records.value: Slow, deaf, harmless, and they come to a hand held still in the water.

records.subject: bond_the_night_valley
records.value: On wet valley ground after dark, his night lift and her standing water make fog that would take a full day-crew a morning — over the one patch of country where no drawer alive can raise anything and at the one hour when no drawer alive works.

records.subject: bond_the_night_valley
records.value: Both of them were told very early that the thing they are best at is the wrong thing to be good at.

world.domain: Atmospheric convection — the real physics that warm air rises only while the ground under it is hotter than the air above, that rising air cools and lets go of its water as haze, cloud and rain, that heat can only be moved and never made, and that cool wet shaded ground never lifts anything at all.
world.progression_means: How much of the day's turn you can work in, and how far you can push the sky away from what it was going to do on its own. Drawers are named for the part of the turn they can work: the cold hour, the climb, the overturn, kept weather.

world.premise:
Ilen Coble is twenty-two and grew up in a fishing town on the coast, where the sea stays warm after dark and the wind turns around at night.

Inland, on the high dry plain, everyone knows the sky only works by day: the sun heats the ground, warm air climbs, and the water in it comes out as haze, cloud and rain. After sundown nothing climbs, so the people who move weather — drawers, they call themselves — stop at dark. Ilen never learned that, because on his coast it is false. At night, on wet ground, he can pull fog thick enough to hide a road.

Drawers are named for how much of the day they can work. Lowest is the cold hour before dawn, when all you can do is pull drinking water out of dry air. Then the climb. Then the overturn, where a man puts a cloud over a dry field at noon and drops a wind out of it that knocks a rider flat. Highest is kept weather, which one woman on the plain has: she can bring rain to country that has none, and has not been warm in nine years, because a drawer cannot make heat, only move it, and it comes out of him.

By day Ilen is at the climb, second of the four, and the worst in his year. The plain has been dry for three years, and he thinks the farmers in the green valley below did it without meaning to.

protagonist.edge: Midnight on the wet flat by the water, and his breath is fogging while nobody else's is. He stands still for a count of two hundred and the fog comes off the ground in sheets and swallows a road, a camp and everybody on it, and inland drawers who have watched him do it three times still say it did not happen.
protagonist.wants: To get to kept weather and put rain back on the plain, and to make the school admit that the rule they beat him with is only true where they happen to live.
protagonist.price: He works at night and sleeps by day, so he misses the daylight training every other student gets and falls further behind them in the one count anybody keeps. His night work is weak — fog and a steady wind, never rain — so nobody who needs rain has any use for him. And it only happens near big water on wet ground, which means leaving the school to do it at all.

systems.name: Drawing
systems.logic: Warm air holds water and cold air cannot. The sun heats the ground, the ground heats the air on it, that air climbs, and as it climbs it cools and lets go of its water as haze, then cloud, then rain. A drawer does not make any of that; a drawer moves heat from where it is to where it is wanted, and starts a lift that then runs on its own. So everything they do is a matter of when — the sky has to already be halfway to doing it.
systems.manifests_as: He kneels on bare stone with both palms flat, and the stone goes cold enough to bead under his hands while a column of dust and grass seed lifts off the ground beside him and keeps climbing.
systems.interface: Over a holder's valley a drawer can do nothing at all. The ground there is shaded, wet and cool, it never gets hot, and air that will not warm will not rise no matter who is standing on it — the refusal is the landscape's, and no amount of talent gets past it. Out on the burnt plain the holders are equally helpless: a drawer can lay hail across a season's work in an afternoon and there is no answer to it. So the whole war is about ground — who gets to keep it green and who gets to keep it bare. A body cannot hold both crafts: a drawer is trained by thirst until they can feel damp in the air, and a holder's hands are in water every day of their life and go dead to it by about fifteen. Children choose at twelve, on the burnt plain, in front of both houses. What a holder can do that no drawer ever can is keep a town alive through a drought, because you cannot make rain out of dry air. What a drawer can do that no holder ever can is end a siege in one afternoon.
systems.hidden_personality: The sky is not fighting anybody. On most days it was already going to do roughly what the drawer took credit for, and every drawer past the climb privately knows this.
systems.view_withholds: Nothing tells a drawer whether the lid is on today. You find out by trying, and by then you have spent the heat.

criterion.evaluates: How much of the day's turn this person can work in, and how far they can push the sky off what it was going to do on its own.

ranks.visible_form: Their forearms and cheeks are wet at dawn when everybody else is dry, and they carry a wide unglazed cup with a permanent cold ring worn into the clay.
ranks.cost_to_reach: A season of thirst. They are given a cup a day until they can feel water in the air, and by the end of it they can find damp ground at a hundred paces and cannot taste salt any more.
ranks.grants: Pull drinking water out of dry air in the hour before dawn — a cup, then a jug, then enough for a family — anywhere, in any drought, with no well and no rain.

ranks.visible_form: Their breath fogs in the middle of the morning when nobody else's does, and the shadows under them go soft and grey while they work.
ranks.cost_to_reach: A winter of holding a lift open on cold days, which is the hard way round. Their hands stop closing properly in the cold for the rest of their life and they eat with the cup in both palms.
ranks.grants: Raise haze and thick fog for as long as the ground is heating: hide a road, hide a march, put a fire out by smothering it, and cool a field enough to save it from a hot wind.

ranks.visible_form: Kites — the great sailing birds that only fly where air is climbing — come and wheel over them within the hour, wherever they are, and everybody for a mile can see it.
ranks.cost_to_reach: They have to take the heat for a full overturn out of themselves rather than out of the ground, once, in front of the school, and be carried off the plain afterwards. And whatever rain they pull is rain that was going to fall on somebody downwind, so they come out of it with a village that knows their name and does not say it kindly.
ranks.grants: Put a real cloud over dry country at noon and pull a downdraft out of it that flattens a rider, dries a flooded field in an hour, or drops hail across a valley's whole season.

ranks.visible_form: They sleep between two fires and are still cold. Frost forms on the inside of a shuttered room where they have been sitting. People bring them their children to be blessed and are not allowed to hand them over.
ranks.cost_to_reach: They never get warm again. No swimming, no held children, no sitting close to anyone, and two fires every night for the rest of their life. And every country downwind of wherever they stand has a reason to want them dead, because rain brought here is rain taken from there.
ranks.grants: Bring rain to country that has none and take it off country that has too much, hold it for days rather than an afternoon, break a siege, end a drought — and be known by name in towns they have never been within a hundred miles of.

rules.rule: Warm air holds water and cold air cannot. Cool warm damp air and the water comes out of it — as dew, then haze, then cloud, then rain. Everything a drawer does is a version of that one move.
rules.manifests_as: She holds the wide cup out at arm's length before dawn and it goes white and streaming with wet, and she drinks without looking at it.

consequences.consequence: Every house on the plain has a thin cold stone set into its roof to catch water, and the youngest child in the house goes up at dawn to wipe it into a jug.
Armies camp on high dry ground where the air has nothing in it, because a camp in a river bottom can be fogged blind by one student.
Dawn is the holy hour and the first cup of the day is poured out on the ground rather than drunk, and a man who drinks his first cup is a man everybody notices.

rules.rule: A drawer cannot make heat. To warm air they take the heat out of something nearby — the ground, a river, or their own body — and that thing goes cold.
rules.manifests_as: He gets up off the stone and the stone has frost on it in the shape of his hands, and two of his year-mates take his elbows without being asked.

consequences.consequence: A drawer can work twice in an afternoon and then has to be carried, so every commander who has one also has two men whose whole job is carrying him.
Drawers are wrapped to the chin in summer, sit closest to every fire, and are not given babies to hold, and everyone on the plain knows one by the wrapping before they know the face.
A town that keeps a drawer loses its warm spring and its fish, so hosting one is argued about in the open, and three towns on the plain have thrown theirs out.

rules.rule: Air only climbs while the ground under it is warmer than the air above. After sundown the ground gives its heat up to the sky and goes cold first, so nothing climbs, and no drawing is possible at night.
rules.manifests_as: The horn goes at dusk, every student on the plain stops where they are and walks in, and the master's shutters close.

consequences.consequence: Every march, every crossing and every assault happens between dusk and dawn, because those are the only hours weather cannot be used on you.
The plain's markets open at sundown and its roads are busiest at midnight, and a stranger travelling by day is either a fool or somebody with a reason.
All training is daylight training and the school shuts at dark, so a student who cannot work mornings simply does not advance, and everybody agrees that is fair.

rules.rule: There is often a warm layer sitting above the ground air like a lid on a pot. While it holds, nothing rises no matter how hard anybody pushes. If it breaks, everything under it goes up at once, by itself, and cannot be stopped by the person who started it.
rules.manifests_as: Two hours of work and nothing at all, and then the whole afternoon sky stands up in one white tower and the drawer who did it starts backing away from it.

consequences.consequence: A siege is planned around lid days, and a commander who guesses wrong loses the day and sometimes the army, because a broken lid does not care whose side it is on.
Lid days are still, close and bad-tempered, and people on the plain say so out loud — fights, thrown crockery and children kept indoors.
Drawers judge each other on whether they can call a lid day before spending themselves on it, and a student who wastes a morning pushing a lid is made to say so in front of the year.

systems.name: Holding
systems.logic: Water put under the ground stays there. Shade it, terrace it, pack the soil and plant over it, and a valley worked this way is green through a drought that empties the country around it. A holder's rule is that a change is only worth making if it costs nothing anybody had — a terrace that saves water but sours the soil is refused outright, and a holder will spend forty years on work that a drawer would do in an afternoon and call it the point.
systems.manifests_as: A woman with her arm in a hole to the shoulder, up to her elbow in cold water, listening; and a valley below her that is green in the third year of a drought.
systems.interface: See the drawing side of it: green wet ground refuses a drawer absolutely, bare hot ground refuses a holder absolutely, and the whole fight is over which kind of ground there is going to be.
systems.hidden_personality: The valley house genuinely believes it is not at war with anybody, which is what makes it dangerous.
systems.view_withholds: A holder cannot see what their work does to the air above it, and has never once thought to ask.

criterion.evaluates: Whether a piece of work is better on every count that matters — water kept, soil held, shade grown, nobody downstream worse off. Work that gains on one count and loses on another is refused, however large the gain.

rules.rule: Water under the ground does not leave. Terraces, shade and packed soil hold it, and a valley worked that way stays green through a drought.
rules.manifests_as: Her hands are white and wrinkled at midday, every day, and she pulls a blind white eel out of a hole, looks at it, and puts it back.

consequences.consequence: Green valleys take in whoever walks in during a dry year, so they have grown from farms into powers, and the plain's towns resent every one of them.
An army cannot burn a wet valley and cannot starve one, so no siege of one has ever worked and commanders have stopped trying.

A holder's hands are in water every day from about eight years old, so by fifteen they can feel nothing in the air at all, and they marry inside the valley because nobody outside it can stand how cold their hands are.

rules.rule: Shaded wet ground does not get hot, and air that does not get hot does not climb. No drawer can raise anything at all above a worked valley.
rules.manifests_as: He stands on the valley road for a whole afternoon with his hands out and absolutely nothing happens, while a girl watches him from a terrace without saying anything.

consequences.consequence: The valley is where anybody hides from a weather war, so every fugitive on the plain is walking downhill and both houses know it.
Drawers can only train out on the burnt plain, which is why the school is where it is, and why every student's first year is spent on ground that takes the skin off their knees.
Holders call rain the wanderer's water and will not drink it, catching from springs only, and they will not take a cup from a drawer's hand.

cast.is_a: Twenty-two, from a fishing town on the coast, first year at the plain school and last in it.
cast.wants: Kept weather, and rain back on the plain.
cast.secret: He has already fogged a night camp on the plain once, on his own, for no reason but to see if he could, and forty men wandered off a road because of it.
cast.false_belief: That if he shows the school what he can do at night, they will change what they teach.
cast.voice_tag: Talks like somebody explaining the tide to a person who has never seen the sea — patient, over-detailed, and slightly too pleased about it.
cast.manifests_as: He looks at the sky before he looks at whoever is speaking to him, and he is always awake at the wrong hours.

relationships.note: She has not thrown him out, which everyone in the year has an opinion about.
Rusk is at the overturn and cannot lose to him by daylight, which is exactly the problem.
She is the only person who has watched him work at night and not immediately told somebody.
She still runs the family boat and writes to him about the wind, which is the only reason he knows the coast's night turn is holding.

cast.is_a: The only drawer alive at kept weather, who runs the school on the burnt plain and has not been warm in nine years.
cast.wants: To find someone who can carry kept weather after her, because both of the two before her walked into the sea.
cast.secret: Her own teacher is alive and being kept comfortable in the green valley, where no weather she can make will ever reach him.
cast.false_belief: That the drought on the plain is the sky's doing and will turn on its own if she outlasts it.
cast.voice_tag: Very quiet, very short, and she says the price of a thing before she says what it does.
cast.manifests_as: Frost on the inside of the shutters of a room she has been sitting in, and two fires burning in her quarters in high summer.

relationships.note: She kept him because she wants to know what the coast knows, and has told him none of that.
He is the school's obvious heir and she has never once said so.
They have her teacher, they have been kind to him for eleven years, and she cannot get to him.

cast.is_a: Twenty-four, at the overturn, first in his year and the best any of them have seen since Tay herself.
cast.wants: To be the one who ends the drought in front of everybody.
cast.secret: He reached the overturn on a day the lid broke on its own, and he knows it, and he has never repeated it cleanly.
cast.false_belief: That Ilen's night work is a trick with damp ground and will be exposed the first time it matters.
cast.voice_tag: Generous in public, exact in private, and he remembers every number anybody has ever posted.
cast.manifests_as: Kites turning over him within the hour, wherever he is standing, and the whole school looking up.

relationships.note: He has offered twice to train him mornings, which was meant kindly and landed as charity.
He has waited four years for her to say it and she has not.
Brask has already paid for his winter, which the school does not know.

cast.is_a: Nineteen, a holder from the green valley, whose hands have been in water every day since she was eight.
cast.wants: To finish her grandmother's terrace line without breaking the house's rule that nothing may be gained at anybody's cost.
cast.secret: She worked out two years ago that the valley's shade is what killed the plain's weather, and has said it to nobody because the house's whole rule depends on it not being true.
cast.false_belief: That she can put it right quietly, on her own, before anybody upstream notices.
cast.voice_tag: Says less than she knows, and answers questions about three seconds late.
cast.manifests_as: White wrinkled fingers at midday and a blind eel going back into its hole.

relationships.note: Night, wet valley ground: the one place and hour where a drawer and a holder are not in each other's way.
Her family have kept the upper springs for six generations and she is the one they expect to keep them next.
For forty miles of shade planted by people who meant nothing but good by it.

cast.is_a: A soldier who has been trying for two years to get a drawer of his own for a siege that a wet valley keeps winning.
cast.wants: An overturn dropped on a valley in one afternoon, and he does not care which house's valley it is.
cast.secret: He has already been told by Tay that hail on a valley is the one thing she will not do, and he has stopped asking her.
cast.false_belief: That weather is a weapon like any other and can be aimed.
cast.voice_tag: Cheerful, direct, buys the drinks, and asks the same question four different ways.
cast.manifests_as: He turns up at the school on lid days, when he knows nobody will be out working.

relationships.note: Paid for his winter and expects an afternoon's work for it.
Twice, in front of witnesses, and he has been polite about it both times.

cast.is_a: Ilen's older sister, who runs the family boat out of the coast town and has never been more than a day inland.
cast.wants: Him home, or at least him useful.
cast.secret: The night wind on their stretch of coast has shifted in the last two years and she has not told him, because he would come back.
cast.false_belief: That the school is a place that will look after him.
cast.voice_tag: Writes the way she talks: weather first, family second, nothing about herself.
cast.manifests_as: A folded letter that starts with which way the wind came round on which night.

relationships.note: Her letters are the only record anybody has of a night turn, and neither of them knows that yet.

institutions.is_a: A low stone compound on the burnt plain where drawers are trained, with a bare stamped field, a well nobody uses, and shutters that close at dusk.
institutions.wants: An heir to kept weather before Tay stops.
institutions.reach: It can send a drawer to any town on the plain, and every town on the plain wants one and can be refused.
institutions.grants: Somebody to warm you and carry you after you have spent yourself, which nobody working alone has.
institutions.prices_the_present: First-year students spend a season being given one cup a day, and about a fifth of them go home.
institutions.manifests_as: A horn at dusk, and forty people stopping mid-stride and walking in.
institutions.secret: They have known for six years that the drought started the same season the valley finished its long shade line, and the master has not said it out loud because saying it starts a war.

relationships.note: Same twelve-year-olds, same week, same patch of burnt ground.
There is no plan for the day after her.

institutions.is_a: The family and the households who keep the green valley's springs — terraces, shade trees, packed channels, and six generations of hands in cold water.
institutions.wants: To finish the shade line to the valley's head, which will take another thirty years and which they consider the work of their lives.
institutions.reach: The valley, everyone who has ever walked into it in a dry year, and the water of four towns downstream.
institutions.grants: Green ground in the third year of a drought, and a place no weather can reach.
institutions.prices_the_present: Their children are in water from eight years old and are deaf to the air by fifteen, and none of them can ever be drawers.
institutions.manifests_as: A green valley you can see from twenty miles out on a plain the colour of ash.
institutions.secret: Their shade line is what killed the plain's lift. They do not know it, they did not mean it, and by their own rule the work would have to be undone.

relationships.note: The one house each considers the reason the other exists.
They have been keeping her old teacher comfortable for eleven years and consider it a kindness.

places.is_a: A high flat of ash-coloured stone and dead grass where the school stands and where children choose at twelve.
places.manifests_as: Knees skinned through the cloth by the second week, and dust devils walking about on their own all afternoon.
places.prices_the_present: Nothing grows here now, so everything the school eats comes up the valley road, and the valley knows it.
places.secret: Old field walls under the dust show it was farmed within living memory.

relationships.note: Built here because it is the only ground that still lifts.

places.is_a: A shaded terraced valley below the plain, green in the third year of a drought, forty miles long.
places.manifests_as: You come over the lip out of white glare into cold air under trees, and everybody who does it stops walking.
places.prices_the_present: A drawer standing in it can do nothing at all, and knows it within about ten minutes.
places.secret: Its shade is the reason the plain above it has no weather.

relationships.note: Six generations, and the shade line is still forty years from finished.

places.is_a: The coast town Ilen comes from: boats, wet flats, and a wind that turns around every night.
places.manifests_as: Fog standing over the water at midnight on a still, clear night, every night, for nothing.
places.prices_the_present: Nobody there has ever thought it was worth mentioning, so no drawer inland has ever heard of it.
places.secret: The night turn there has been weakening for two years, and Sura has not written it down.

relationships.note: He has not been back in a year and has stopped saying when he will.

agencies.is_a: The sea, which keeps its heat long after the land has given up.
agencies.recognises: Anybody standing on wet ground within reach of it after dark.
agencies.reach: The coast and, on a still night, some forty miles inland.
agencies.grants: Lift at night, where the whole inland world says there is none.
agencies.prices_the_present: What it gives is small — fog and a steady breeze, never rain — and it gives it only where it is, so anybody who wants it has to go and stand there.
agencies.false_belief: Every drawer inland believes night lift is a story coastal people tell.
agencies.manifests_as: His breath fogging at midnight while nobody else's does.
agencies.secret: It has been giving less every year for two years running.

relationships.note: Barely, now, and only on the stillest nights.

agencies.is_a: A warm layer that sits over the ground air, some days, and holds everything under it down.
agencies.recognises: Nobody. It is on or it is not.
agencies.reach: Whole countries at once, for a day or a week.
agencies.grants: When it breaks, more than any drawer alive could have started on their own, all at once and out of anybody's hands.
agencies.prices_the_present: On a lid day the best drawer in the world is a wrapped-up person sitting by a fire, and everybody's temper is short.
agencies.false_belief: Students believe the lid is something a strong enough drawer can push through.
agencies.manifests_as: Two hours of nothing, and then the whole sky standing up in one white tower while the person who started it walks backwards away from it.
agencies.secret: A lid over the plain has held for most of three years, which is not weather, and Tay has half worked out why.

relationships.note: It has barely lifted since the shade line was finished.

history.is_a: The night, eighty years back, when a coastal drawer fogged the burnt plain in the dark and nearly killed the school's founder in the confusion.
history.reach: Every student who has ever been told to stop work at dusk.
history.prices_the_present: No coastal student has been taken since, and the rule against night work is taught as physics rather than as a grudge.
history.false_belief: Everyone at the school believes the dusk rule was written because nothing can be done at night.
history.manifests_as: A horn at dusk and a master who will not explain why the horn exists.
history.secret: The founder wrote the rule knowing full well the coast is an exception, and wrote it anyway.

relationships.note: It is the oldest rule in the place and the only one nobody may ask about.

creatures.is_a: Great sailing birds, wider than a man is tall, that cannot flap far and so can only fly where air is climbing.
creatures.mechanism: They hang inside a rising column and are carried up it, then glide out and look for the next one, all day, without a wingbeat.
creatures.ecology: They circle over bare hot ground and never once over the green valley, and their range has shrunk with the plain's lift for three years running.
creatures.human_use: Drawers read them. Where kites are turning, the sky will work; first-years are sent up a hill at dawn to watch and count them, and a drawer who is working well can be found from miles away by the wheel of birds over him.
creatures.behaviour: Utterly indifferent to people, and they will land beside a drawer who holds a column open, close enough to touch, for as long as it stays open.
creatures.manifests_as: Eleven birds turning in a slow wheel over a bare hill, all the same way round, and a boy on a wall counting them out loud.
creatures.bond_potential: A drawer at the overturn can hold a column open where they choose and put kites there, which is how a signal is sent across a plain in an afternoon.

creatures.is_a: Black flies the size of a grain that hatch in the hours before rain.
creatures.mechanism: They come out of the ground when the air goes light and thin, which happens ahead of weather.
creatures.ecology: They lie in the soil for years and hatch on the plain perhaps twice a year now, where it used to be twenty.
creatures.human_use: Everybody's warning. A black smear along the ground means shutters closed and washing in by evening, and the plain's children are paid a coin a cup for them.
creatures.behaviour: They get into the eyes and the mouth and they do not bite, which is somehow worse.
creatures.manifests_as: A black smear crawling along a road at ankle height, and every window on the street banging shut behind it.

creatures.is_a: Blind white eels, arm-long, that live in the water under the valley.
creatures.mechanism: They cannot survive in moving water and die within a day if the ground water starts to run.
creatures.ecology: They exist only under worked valleys and have followed the holders' terracing for six generations.
creatures.human_use: Holders read them: a hole with a fat eel in it is water that has been standing quietly for years, and a hole with none is a warning that something upstream has been cut.
creatures.behaviour: Slow, deaf, harmless, and they come to a hand held still in the water.
creatures.manifests_as: A girl with her arm in a hole to the shoulder, drawing out something long and white, looking at it, and putting it back.

bonds.joint_ability: On wet valley ground after dark, his night lift and her standing water make fog that would take a full day-crew a morning — over the one patch of country where no drawer alive can raise anything and at the one hour when no drawer alive works.
bonds.trait_link: Both of them were told very early that the thing they are best at is the wrong thing to be good at.

mysteries.question: Why has the plain school never once taken a student from the coast?
mysteries.answer: Because eighty years ago a coastal drawer fogged the burnt plain at night and nearly killed the school's founder in the dark, and the founder wrote the dusk rule in response — knowing perfectly well that the coast is an exception to it. The rule is a grudge dressed as physics, and it is only true inland.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Every student at the school, who has been taught the dusk rule as a plain fact about air.

mysteries.question: Where did the plain's three-year drought come from?
mysteries.answer: The valley house finished a forty-mile shade line, which keeps the valley floor cool and wet, so the air coming up onto the plain never warms enough to climb. The drought is manmade, nobody aimed it, and by the holders' own rule — that no work may cost anybody anything — the shade line would have to come down.
mysteries.believed_instead_by: Master Tay, who believes it is the sky's own turn and can be outlasted; and the valley house, who believe they have never harmed anybody.

mysteries.question: What does the highest of the four actually cost, and what happened to the two before Tay?
mysteries.answer: Never being warm again — no swimming, no held children, two fires every night for life. Both of the drawers before her walked into the sea, and Tay knows exactly why they did it and has already picked the year she will.

mysteries.question: Who is Master Tay afraid of?
mysteries.answer: Her own teacher, who is alive, comfortable, and eleven years a guest of the valley house — in the one place on earth where nothing she can make will ever reach him. He went willingly, and he went because of what she did to a village downwind.

directives.text: Fast, plain, popcorn prose. The sky is described by what it does to people standing under it, never by how it works.

No technical vocabulary from the real physics reaches the page. Nobody says convection, humidity, latent heat, inversion, thermal or dew point. The page's words are climb, lift, lid, the turn, cold hour, going cold.

No debts, no registers, no filed papers, no courts, no tariffs. Every price is paid in cold, in thirst, in hours slept at the wrong time, in something a person can no longer do, or in a village downwind that now knows their name.
The first twelve scenes run from Ilen being counted last on the burnt plain to him fogging something on a night that matters, and settle why the school has never taken a coastal student.
End chapters on somebody paying, or on the sky doing something nobody meant.
